q1_issues.issue: "The mire-essence in the lanterns held salt-bloom" is a containment stative transitive, which the instruction set assigns Agent (its own example "the tank holds forty litres"), reserving Holder for own/have/lack only.

The of-phrase restrictor in "the keepers of the Middle Row" is dropped entirely — sk_keeper_1 gets no Possession/PartOf link to middle_row, although the parallel "the lanterns of the Middle Row" does get one.

"The lanterns stayed lit" emits only the per-member reified-state rule; the mandated flat half of the continuation-copular dual-emit (as the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lantern_1) (Member $x lit))) is missing, so no member's "is it lit?" can bind.
"left silken threads" takes Patient although depositing leaves the threads unchanged — the change test (and its default-to-Theme fallback) selects Theme.
(Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 1 cauldron) puts the entity's own class in the scale slot, which the instruction set licenses only for an associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension.

"boiled ... in sea-water" is slotted as Instrument although the PP answers "where/in what medium" and its preposition is "in", where the instruction set's oblique rules point to Location or the preposition-named (In ...).

q2_gaps: ordinal day-of-year dating ("on day 460 of Year 2") — (Day <n>) is defined only as the day-of-month granularity of a calendar expression, leaving a day numbered within the year with no distinct licensed form
an ordinal that ranks a plain object noun with no associated event and no "-est" dimension ("the first cauldron") — the instruction set supplies no licensed filler for Ordinal's scale slot

a distributive per-member rule whose predicate is TRANSITIVE with a plural/group object ("the keepers lit the lanterns", "the nightmoths left silken threads") — every distributive example given is intransitive, and the instruction set never says whether the object distributes too, so the shared-symbol convention yields "each keeper lit the whole lantern group"

cross-part-of-speech lemma collision — "lit" (verb) and "mist-light" (noun head) both lemmatize to the symbol light, and the instruction set offers no sense-disambiguation, so the lighting event class and the noun genus share one symbol
notes: Aside from the role and dual-emit slips above the passage is well tracked — witness identity (two distinct keeper groups, two distinct mire-essence witnesses), the compound decompositions (silken_thread with its material-adjective modifier genus, clay_vessel and nightmoth without noun-modifier genera), "by evening" as TimeAtMost, and the creation/positioning events correctly taking Location on the event only. One further omission: the participial modifier in "the stored mire-essence" gets no atom, though coreference to sk_mire_essence_2 arguably discharges it.
